answer: Sybil attacks fail when identity costs real verifiable work, not cheap key generation. Each agent must answer an epoch challenge graded by a randomly sampled audit committee, drawn with a Yarrow-seeded verifiable beacon so no attacker can predict or stack the panel. The grading kernel caps every identity to a single attestation weight, so spinning up a thousand hollow clones buys no extra voice; they still converge to one honest signal at each consensus summit.
